name: Emami Ltd
title: Emami Ltd-$ - 531162 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Emami Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell 4% to INR925 crores and EBITDA 15% to INR187 crores, as a delayed summer hit talc; gross margin rose 250 bps to 68.4%.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR925 crores, down 4% YoY, which management attributed mainly to a delayed summer and a high prior-year base rather than structural weakness. Summer portfolio fell 22% (talc down 40%), while ex-summer domestic business grew 11%. Gross margin expanded 250 bps to 68.4%, but EBITDA fell 15% to INR187 crores on operating deleverage and higher ad spends (up 12%); PAT fell 12% to INR143 crores. For FY26, revenue was INR3,780 crores (down 1%), EBITDA INR964 crores (down 6%) and PAT INR775 crores (down 4%). International business declined 5% in the quarter due to Middle East disruption.

financial_highlights.metric: Advertising and promotion spend Q4 FY26
financial_highlights.value: grew 12%; about 22-23% of sales per analyst

financial_highlights.change: 10 days improvement in working capital cycle

segments.name: Domestic ex-summer portfolio
segments.commentary: Grew 11% in Q4 FY26. Pain Management +11%, Kesh King +14% (second straight double-digit quarter), Healthcare +7%, 7 Oils in One +34%, BoroPlus ex-talc +4%, Male Grooming -4%.

segments.name: Summer portfolio
segments.commentary: Declined 22% in Q4 FY26, with talc down 40%. Talc revenue was about INR300 crores in FY26, versus about INR400 crores before FY25, a loss of about INR100 crores.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Declined 5% in Q4 FY26 due to Middle East disruption (Strait of Hormuz shipping, freight costs, supply chains across GCC, CIS and South Asia). Growth was near double digits before 28 February 2026; April 2026 was about +2%.

segments.name: Strategic investments
segments.commentary: Grew 34% in Q4 FY26. Management targets 30% YoY growth and about INR15 crores increase in absolute EBITDA this year. Axiom (aloe vera fruit drink) is profitable, with EBITDA of about INR40-45 crores cited. IncNut (Vedix, SkinKraft) runs high gross margins with modest EBITDA losses.

segments.name: Channels
segments.commentary: Organized channels rose to about 32% of domestic business; wholesale fell to 27%. Quick Commerce grew 70% and GT Marts grew 25%.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of a strong summer in H1 FY27, with Navratna and Dermicool expected to grow at double digits; no BoroPlus forecast given.
International: April 2026 about +2%; May and June expected to stabilise; Q1 FY27 close to single-digit growth; good double-digit growth from Q2 FY27.
Strategic investments targeted to grow 30%+ YoY while improving bottom line; intent to add about INR15 crores absolute EBITDA this year.
Margins expected to improve, but input cost pressure from crude remains; no explicit EBITDA margin target given, though analyst cited a prior 26-27% consolidated EBITDA range.
Weighted average price increase of about 3% taken over the last 1.5-2 months.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or utilisation figures discussed in the call.
Distribution reach of about 500,000 outlets across urban and rural India and about 100,000 towns covered; focus is on GT Marts, premium and upgraded stores in urban India.
Axiom: new CEO hired from Dabur (former Head of Nepal business); management says large growth plans exist.
demand_pricing: Delayed and inconsistent summer plus unseasonal rain weighed on Q4 demand; management says summer is running strong in April-May with some markets seeing double-digit growth.
Hair oil: management attributes strength in Kesh King and 7 Oils in One partly to unorganised players becoming unviable on higher costs, plus BCG-led brand strategy.
Ad spend is about 19.6% of FY26 sales: about 14% on the existing portfolio and about 6% on investee companies. The Q4 spike was mainly Brillare (Rosemary oil launch).
Management says the new channels are now close to GT margins, and large packs were introduced in modern trade and e-commerce.
Analyst flagged GT volume pressure as new channels grow above 30%; management cited distributor hygiene and credit discipline.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Navratna Dermicool in Q1-Q2 given rain, and BoroPlus growth in FY27 after a weak Q4 (-8%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is very confident of double-digit growth for summer brands in H1 FY27. It gave no BoroPlus forecast, noting a lower base helps but winter outcome is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Can the new and mainstream portfolio (about 21% of business) grow 25-30% annually; why did IncNut stagnate?
qa_highlights.answer: Dhruv Aggarwal said the portfolio can grow 30%+ YoY, with Q4 growth faster than the rest of the year. IncNut's margins have turned, and efficiency and Vedix international opportunities are the levers.

qa_highlights.question: Is Axiom's right to win intact given competition from Campa Cola?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohan Goenka said Axiom is aloe vera based and differentiated, earning about INR40-45 crores EBITDA; a new CEO from Dabur has joined.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the hair oil growth over the last two quarters, and does copra price easing matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited unorganised players becoming unviable on cost, plus BCG-led relaunch of Kesh King and 7 Oils in One. It said it does not track copra prices.

qa_highlights.question: Are new channels less profitable than traditional channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new-channel margins have improved and are now close to GT margins; organised channels are about 32% of domestic sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why are ad spends about 22-23% of sales, and what share goes to core brands versus growth initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: The Q4 spike was mainly Brillare. For FY26, ad spend was 19.6% of sales: about 14% on the existing portfolio and 6% on investee companies.

qa_highlights.question: How much did talc hurt FY26, and can summer drive another spike?
qa_highlights.answer: Talc is about 10% of revenue (about INR300 crores in FY26, down about INR100 crores). Ex-summer growth is about 5%. Talc carries slightly lower margins than the rest of the range.

qa_highlights.question: Will consolidated EBITDA margin return to 26-27%, and what price increase was taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said input cost pressure from crude remains, so margins should improve but it would wait and watch. A weighted average price increase of about 3% was taken in the last 1.5-2 months.

risks_watch: Middle East disruption: Strait of Hormuz, freight and supply chain costs continue to weigh on international business, which is about 30% of GCC supply sourced from Europe.
Summer dependence: talc and summer brands drove the swing; a weak or late summer again would hit growth.
Input costs: crude-linked costs still pressure margins; EBITDA margin recovery to earlier levels is not yet assured.
Winter and El Nino: possible weak winter in FY27 for BoroPlus, which has no forecast.
Strategic investments: IncNut sales were stagnant over three years, and Axiom faces more competition after Campa Cola's entry; both still loss-making or small.
Distributor health in GT channels as new channels grow faster.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on FY27 and the domestic core, but openly acknowledged a difficult Q4 and international headwinds. It was more guarded on BoroPlus, input costs and the margin path, and deflected the copra question.
key_quotes: This decline was primarily driven by weak summer rather than any structural or competitive weakness in our business.
Overall, we are very confident in the first half, the summer brands definitely growing at double digits, both Navratna and Dermicool.
Talc for the total business should be roughly at about 10%.

growth.why: Management guides investee companies to sustain 30% YoY growth and add about INR15 crores absolute EBITDA in FY27, plus international to grow good double digits from Q2 FY27 and a strong H1 summer; backing is demand signals, a ~3% price increase and new channels, with no capacity, order or contract numbers given.
